solutions.latex: The points show a strong negative linear correlation, so the best estimate is $-0.9$.
A shift of 3 units to the left is a horizontal translation, giving $y=f(x+3)$.
High tide to low tide is half a period, so the period is $T=12$. Using $T=\dfrac{2\pi}{n}$, $n=\dfrac{2\pi}{T}=\dfrac{2\pi}{12}=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

$\dfrac{dx}{dt}=3t^2+\dfrac{6t^2}{2t^3+1}$. Stationary when $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=0$: $3t^2(2t^3+1)+6t^2=0$, so $3t^2(2t^3+3)=0$. Then $t=0$ or $t=-\sqrt[3]{\tfrac32}$, and only $t=0$ is valid for $t\ge0$. One solution.

Area $=\dfrac12ab\sin\theta$: $16=\dfrac12\times8\times8\sin\theta$, so $\sin\theta=\dfrac12$ and $\theta=30^\circ$ or $150^\circ$ (the angle at $A$). Then $\angle ABC=\dfrac{30^\circ}{2}=15^\circ$ or $\dfrac{150^\circ}{2}=75^\circ$.

$[f(x)]^2-[g(x)]^2=[f(x)+g(x)][f(x)-g(x)]=0$. $f(x)+g(x)=0$ only when $f(x)=g(x)=0$, at $x=1$. $f(x)-g(x)=0$ means $f(x)=g(x)$, i.e. at the points of intersection. One of these is $x=1$, already counted, and there is one other point of intersection. So there are 2 solutions.

solutions.question: 13(a)
solutions.latex:
Surface area $A=2(xy+2x+2y)=2xy+4x+4y$. Substituting $y=\dfrac3x$: $A=4x+\dfrac{12}{x}+6$.

$\dfrac{dA}{dx}=4-\dfrac{12}{x^2}$. Minimum area when $\dfrac{dA}{dx}=0$: $4x^2=12$, $x^2=3$, $x=\sqrt3$ (since $x>0$).

Test: $\dfrac{d^2A}{dx^2}=\dfrac{24}{x^3}>0$ for all $x>0$, so concave up and the area is a minimum at $x=\sqrt3$. Then $y=\dfrac{3}{\sqrt3}=\sqrt3$.

Dimensions of tank: $\sqrt3\times\sqrt3\times2$ (no penalty for not writing a dimension statement).
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: correct dimensions with justification of minimum; 2: correct $x$ found; 1: correct $\frac{dA}{dx}$

solutions.question: 15(a)
solutions.latex:
Since $\ln X=0$ when $X=1$: $2\sin^2\theta-\cos\theta=1$, so $2(1-\cos^2\theta)-\cos\theta-1=0$, giving $2\cos^2\theta+\cos\theta-1=0$ and $(2\cos\theta-1)(\cos\theta+1)=0$.

So $\cos\theta=\dfrac12$ or $\cos\theta=-1$. For $0\le\theta\le2\pi$: $\theta=\dfrac\pi3,\ \pi,\ \dfrac{5\pi}3$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 4: all three solutions; 3: correct quadratic factorised and values of cos found; 2: correct quadratic in cos; 1: $2\sin^2\theta-\cos\theta=1$

solutions.question: 15(b)
solutions.latex:
$y'=4x^3-6x^2$, $y''=12x^2-12x$.

Stationary points: $4x^3-6x^2=0$, $2x^2(2x-3)=0$, so $x=0$ or $x=\dfrac32$.

At $x=0$: $y''=0$, a possible horizontal point of inflexion. At $x=\dfrac32$: $y''=9>0$, concave up, so a minimum turning point at $\left(\dfrac32,-0.6875\right)=\left(\dfrac32,-\dfrac{11}{16}\right)$.

Possible points of inflexion when $y''=0$: $12x(x-1)=0$, so $x=0$ or $x=1$. Testing concavity: $y''=24$ at $x=-1$, $0$ at $x=0$, $-3$ at $x=0.5$, $0$ at $x=1$, $24$ at $x=2$. So there is a horizontal point of inflexion at $(0,1)$ and a point of inflexion at $(1,0)$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 4: all points found and nature justified; includes 1 for correct stationary $x$-values, 1 for correct test for the minimum, 1 for correct possible inflexion $x$-values, 1 for correctly identifying the points of inflexion

solutions.question: 15(c)
solutions.latex:
Total vertical distance for each bounce is twice its height, plus the first 2 m, so this is a limiting sum of a G.P. (subtracting the initial 2 m).

Moon: $a=2$, $r=0.95$: $D_{\text{Moon}}=\dfrac{2}{1-0.95}-2=78$ metres.

Earth: $a=2$, $r=0.5$: $D_{\text{Earth}}=\dfrac{2}{1-0.5}-2=6$ metres.

Difference $=78-6=72$ metres.

Alternatively, if students neglect the initial bounce-up and find $80-8=72$ m, award full marks (with correct working).
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: correct difference; 1: correct Moon distance; 1: correct Earth distance

solutions.question: 16(a)
solutions.latex:
$y'=\cos x$. At $x=h$, gradient $=\cos h$.

Tangent: $y-\sin h=\cos h\,(x-h)$, so $y=(\cos h)x-h\cos h+\sin h$.

The tangent passes through the origin $(0,0)$: $0=0-h\cos h+\sin h$, so $h\cos h=\sin h$ and $h=\dfrac{\sin h}{\cos h}=\tan h$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 4: complete proof; 1: derivative; 1: equation of tangent; 1: substitution of the origin; 1: final result

solutions.question: 18(b)
solutions.latex:
Lower rectangle areas $<\displaystyle\int_1^2\dfrac{dx}{2x}<$ upper rectangle areas.

At $x=1$, $y=\dfrac12$; at $x=1.5$, $y=\dfrac13$; at $x=2$, $y=\dfrac14$.

Lower rectangles: $\dfrac13\times\dfrac12+\dfrac14\times\dfrac12=\dfrac7{24}$. Upper rectangles: $\dfrac12\times\dfrac12+\dfrac13\times\dfrac12=\dfrac5{12}$.

$\displaystyle\int_1^2\dfrac{dx}{2x}=\dfrac12\left[\ln x\right]_1^2=\dfrac12(\ln2-\ln1)=\dfrac12\ln2=\ln\sqrt2$.

Hence $\dfrac7{24}<\ln\sqrt2<\dfrac5{12}$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: complete proof; 1: both rectangle sums correct; 1: integral evaluated to $\ln\sqrt2$; 1: conclusion
